:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
$$
\iint\limits_{D} \boxed{ {\phantom{A A A A A A A A}}} \: \text{d}A, 
\qquad D= \{ (u,v) \: : \:  0 \leq u \leq 3, \: 0 \leq v \leq 2 \}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u, \: v, \: u^3-v \big\rangle$ for $0 \leq u \leq 3$ and $0 \leq v \leq 2.$ What is the missing expression?
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf r (u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \,\textrm d S = \iint\limits_D  \left\|  \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \right\|  \text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3{u}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨-3{u}^{2},\,1,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and its magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-3{u}^{2},\,1,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(3{u}^{2})^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{u}^{4}+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{9{u}^{4}+2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡v & 1 \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}3\operatorname{cos}⁡v & 1 \\ -3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 0\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 1 \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & 0\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & 3\operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-6u{sin}^{2}⁡v-6u{cos}^{2}⁡v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-6u⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-6u⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v)^{2}+(2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)^{2}+(-6u)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v)+4{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v)+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+4{u}^{2}+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡v+40{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡v+8)} \\  & =\sqrt{5{u}^{2}}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡v+8} \\  & =\sqrt{5}u\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡v+8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{u}^{2}}=u$ since $u\ge 0$ on $D.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{5}u\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡v+8}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2v,\,2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 2u & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2v & 2v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ -2v & 2v\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}2u & 1 \\ 0 & -2v\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨2v,\,-4uv,\,-4uv⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2v,\,-4uv,\,-4uv⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2v)^{2}+(-4uv)^{2}+(-4uv)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}+32{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}(1+8{u}^{2})} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}}\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}} \\  & =2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{v}^{2}}=v$ since $v\ge 0$ on $D.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2v\sqrt{1+8{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & v \\ 0 & 2v & u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & v \\ 2v & u\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}2u & v \\ 0 & u\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-2{u}^{2},\,4uv⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-2{u}^{2},\,4uv⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-2{v}^{2})^{2}+(-2{u}^{2})^{2}+(4uv)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{4}+4{u}^{4}+16{u}^{2}{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({u}^{4}+{v}^{4}+4{u}^{2}{v}^{2})} \\  & =2\sqrt{{u}^{4}+{v}^{4}+4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\sqrt{{u}^{4}+{v}^{4}+4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$
